item.title: Katy Perry Condemns Trump Administration’s Use of ‘Firework’ in Military Strikes Video
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: "Welcome to this week's trending news on Billboard. I'm your host, and today we're talking about Katy Perry. The pop star is speaking out against the White House for using her hit song 'Firework' without permission.
[Short music clip of "Firework" plays]
Host: "The White House posted a TikTok video featuring footage of military strikes, set to Perry's 2010 anthem. But Perry was not happy about it. She took to social media to condemn the use of her song, saying she did not approve it and absolutely does not condone it.
[Short pause]
Host: "Perry wrote that she created 'Firework' as an anthem of hope, healing, and inner strength, and that seeing it used to soundtrack destruction and violence is a complete violation of what her song stands for. She emphasized that her music is for bringing people together, not celebrating warfare.
[Short music clip of "Firework" plays]
Host: "This isn't the first time an artist has spoken out against the Trump administration for using their music without permission. Ariana Grande and Kesha have also criticized the White House for using their songs in similar contexts.
[Outro music plays]
Host: "That's the latest from Billboard. Thanks for tuning in. Katy Perry's 'Firework' may be a song of hope and empowerment, but it's clear that the pop star won't let it be used to perpetuate violence or destruction."
